subject: environmental-science
title: Ecosystem Services and Trophic Dynamics
welcome_lead: Pollination, carbon storage and pest control — nature's hidden balance sheet.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on ecosystem services, energy flow and ecological efficiency.
final_note: Every trophic transfer wastes roughly 90% — efficiency is the currency of ecology.

concepts.def: Tangible products: food, fibre, freshwater, fuel.
Processes moderating environmental conditions: climate, flood and disease regulation.
Underlying processes such as nutrient cycling and primary production.
Total energy fixed by producers via photosynthesis (kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹).
Proportion of energy transferred between trophic levels, typically ~10%.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005) groups services into provisioning, regulating, supporting and cultural — used widely in EIA.
NPP = GPP − R. Losses at each transfer (heat, respiration, egestion) limit food chains to ~4–5 links.
Costanza et al. valued global ecosystem services at ~US$125 trillion yr⁻¹ (2014), exceeding global GDP.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.
About 50 percent.

100 percent (everything transfers).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?

About 50 percent.
They are the same measurement.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
